carpet.rule.potionDupe.desc: Brings back the 1.21.1 potion duplication: a thrown potion that goes through a nether portal still splashes in the old dimension
carpet.rule.potionDupe.extra.0: Uses the 1.21.1 projectile tick order, honey block sliding, hit margin and 300 tick portal cooldown
carpet.rule.potionDupeScope.extra.0: potions: splash and lingering potions, all: every thrown projectile except ender pearls
carpet.rule.potionDupeHitAfterPortal.des: potionDupe part: the projectile still hits in the tick it went through a portal
carpet.rule.potionDupeLegacyPortalCooldo: potionDupe part: 300 tick portal cooldown for projectiles (1.21.2+ uses 2)
carpet.rule.potionDupeLegacyPhysics.desc: potionDupe part: 1.21.1 tick order, honey block sliding and hit margin
carpet.rule.lightSuppression.desc: Lets old light suppressors work: the light engine handles only a limited number of light tasks per tick
carpet.rule.lightSuppression.extra.0: A machine that makes more light updates than that builds up a queue, so other light updates wait behind it
carpet.rule.lightSuppression.extra.1: Light updates still queued when the server stops are lost, as in old versions. New chunks load a bit slower while a backlog exists (the budget is 10x while the server waits for a chunk)
carpet.rule.lightSuppressionTasksPerTick: Light tasks handled per tick (50 ms) while lightSuppression is on (rounded up to batches of 1000)
Lower makes suppressors easier to build, higher keeps normal lighting faster
